title: Grill round 2 — Issue #298: vendored terminfo + card keys
summary:
Round 1 answered all 13 questions, but two answers need a precise follow-up before Planning:

1. **`terminfo-source`** chose **`vendor-db`** (overriding the recommendation of the system DB). The plan now needs to know **which entries**, **from where**, and **whether they are committed or generated** — otherwise the build step is unspecified.
2. **`card-presentation`** chose **both `keep-keys` and `hide-keys`**, which are mutually exclusive for the Chrome card. The plan needs the actual rule, because hiding keys adds a field to the prompt plumbing.

The other 11 answers are settled and are **not** re-asked: `both-one-commit`, `generic-strict`, `card-only`, `attach-bundled`, `await-502-stay-open`, `no-dismiss`, `units-manual`, plus the four confirms (docs, commit, keep the unparsable fallback, no cross-agent arbitration).

proven.text: **The system terminfo DB is 6.4 MB / 2,684 files; the five entries the app actually uses are ~12 KB.** Verified on macOS 26.6.2: `/usr/share/terminfo/<hex>/xterm-256color` (3,462 B), `xterm` (3,412 B), `screen` (1,587 B), `screen-256color` (1,912 B), `tmux-256color` (2,010 B). `infocmp -A /usr/share/terminfo` resolves all five.

**The vendor tree is a generated, gitignored build product.** `vendor` is ignored (`.gitignore:15`), `bun run vendor:tmux` populates `vendor/tmux/arm64/`, and `electrobun.config.ts:53` copies that whole directory to `Contents/Resources/app/bin/`. A sibling `terminfo/` under the vendor dir therefore lands at `<bundle>/bin/terminfo`, next to `<bundle>/bin/tmux`.

proven.text: **`TERMINFO_DIRS` is a search path, not a single dir.** The helper can point at `<bundle>/bin/terminfo` first and `/usr/share/terminfo` second, so a custom `TERM` that is not in the minimal set still resolves from the OS DB. The packaged bundle needs the first entry; a dev checkout without the vendor tree can use the second alone.

**Hiding the synthetic keys is a contained plumbing change, not a new interaction kind.** The card renders `${key}. ${label}`; a `hideKeys` flag would ride `ScrapeMatch` → `TmuxPromptRequest` → the hand-mirrored `PendingTmuxPrompt` in `api.ts` → `TmuxPromptCard`. Numbered prompts keep their real numbers; only the unnumbered menu hides them.

sections.title: Vendored terminfo
sections.intro: You chose the vendored DB. These are the two build decisions that choice leaves open.

questions.title: Which terminfo entries should the vendored DB contain, and from where?
questions.why: The plan needs a concrete copy list and source; a full DB is 6.4 MB and 2,684 files, while the five entries the app uses are ~12 KB.
questions.context: The bundled tmux is 3.6a linked against Homebrew ncurses 6.5. The reported Terminal.app profile uses `xterm-256color`; tmux clients use `screen-256color` / `tmux-256color`. The system DB has all five entries. A `TERMINFO_DIRS` search path can put the vendored dir first and `/usr/share/terminfo` second, so a custom `TERM` outside the minimal set still resolves when the OS DB exists.

options.label: Five entries from the macOS system DB
options.consequence: Covers the reported Terminal.app and tmux clients; custom TERMs fall back to `/usr/share/terminfo` via the search path. The smallest, most auditable vendor.

options.label: The same five entries from the bundled ncurses Cellar DB
options.consequence: Matches the library exactly, but the source is the build machine's Homebrew and must be located robustly (the same Cellar path that caused the bug).

options.label: The whole `/usr/share/terminfo` tree
options.consequence: Every stock TERM works with no OS dependency; a much larger bundle and a bigger generated tree.

options.label: The ncurses release's terminfo DB
options.description: Vendored from the ncurses source/release, with its license.
options.consequence: Reproducible across build machines; the most build work and a new upstream artifact to track.

recommendation.reason: ~12 KB covers the app's terminals, and the runtime search path keeps the OS DB as a secondary source for custom TERMs.

questions.title: Should the vendored terminfo files be committed, or generated by `bun run vendor:tmux`?
questions.why: Decides whether the plan adds files to git or a build step, and how a dev checkout without the vendor tree behaves.
questions.context: `vendor/tmux/arm64` is already gitignored and generated by `bun run vendor:tmux`; the script caches on the tmux binary's mtime and signing identity, so it must also check the terminfo dir. A missing vendored dir should not break dev: the runtime helper can fall back to `/usr/share/terminfo`.

options.label: Generate it into the vendor tree (gitignored)
options.description: `bun run vendor:tmux` copies the chosen entries into `vendor/tmux/arm64/terminfo`; a missing dir falls back to `/usr/share/terminfo`.
options.consequence: Consistent with the existing vendor tree; a macOS build host is required; dev checkouts without the vendor tree still work.

options.label: Commit the terminfo files
options.description: Un-ignore the terminfo subdir and check in the entries (plus a license/provenance note).
options.consequence: Every checkout builds identically; adds a small binary-ish tree to git and a deliberate update step if the entries change.

recommendation.reason: The vendor tree is already generated and gitignored; the fallback keeps dev builds working without it.

recommendation.value: Yes — add the ncurses/terminfo license text and a one-line provenance note (source path + date) next to the vendored DB.
recommendation.reason: The terminfo entries come from ncurses; shipping the license and the source is cheap and keeps the bundle reviewable.

sections.title: Card keys
sections.intro: Round 1 selected both options; this resolves which one the build uses.

questions.title: You picked both 'keep the numbered-button convention' and 'hide the synthetic keys' — which rule should the unnumbered card follow?
questions.why: The two options are mutually exclusive for the Chrome card; hiding keys adds a `hideKeys` field to the prompt plumbing.
questions.context: The generic card renders `1. No…` / `2. Yes…`. For the unnumbered Chrome dialog the real TUI has no numbers. Keeping the convention means no new flag; hiding means threading `hideKeys` through `ScrapeMatch` → `TmuxPromptRequest` → `api.ts` → `TmuxPromptCard`. Numbered prompts (permission modals, sliders) always have real digits and are unaffected by the rule.

options.label: Hide keys only for unnumbered menus
options.description: Add `hideKeys`; numbered prompts keep their `1.`/`2.` labels.
options.consequence: The Chrome card matches the real dialog; one new optional field and its tests. This is the only reading that honors both round-1 picks.

options.label: Keep the synthetic keys on every card
options.description: No new flag; the Chrome card shows `1.`/`2.`.
options.consequence: Lower surface, but the numbers do not exist in the TUI.

options.label: Hide keys on every choice card
options.consequence: Simplest rule, but it hides real digits the user could type in the terminal.

recommendation.reason: It honors both round-1 picks: keep the numbered convention where the TUI really has numbers, hide the synthetic ones where it does not.
